source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length2_29/training_1.csv"

merged["rating"] = merged["rating"].astype(int)

# Assign to target table name
Target2_29 = merged[["movie title", "movie id", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating"]]

# Write the result to the specified path

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_29/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_29/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source2_29_0 and Source2_29_1 on movie id = movie_id
joined = pd.merge(source0, source1, left_on="movie id", right_on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Group by movie title (the primary key) and aggregate other columns by max to ensure uniqueness and match target keys
result = joined.groupby("movie title", as_index=False).agg({
    "movie id": "max",
    "user_id": "max",
    "movie_id": "max",
    "rating": "max"
})

# Write the final output with exact target schema and column order
result = result[["movie title", "movie id", "user_id", "movie_id", "rating"]]
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_29/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
